pages.text: Today they would press olives for oil. Beside the barn stood a big round stone. Turn it, and it crushed olives to release their oil.
Lulu crouched by the stone. "I will see the first drop."
Uncle Beppo held the long wooden handle. "In our day, I could turn it alone."
He pushed with a grunt. The stone did not budge.
"Urrgh!" He pushed until his face was red. Still nothing.
He hung from the handle, feet dangling. Still no turning.
He dusted his palms and stared at the stone.
Lulu took the handle's end. "Everyone, push together!" The cousins, Uncle Nino, and Aunt Rosa joined.
Lulu pulled at the front, and everyone pushed behind. Rumble! The stone slowly began to turn.
Drip! The first drop fell. Lulu saw it first. Uncle Beppo chuckled. "Yes! In our day, we all turned it together!"
